status: draft: written for the v1.4.0 kind recall gate; awaiting Amr's sign-off
source: public analytics practice on a public Databricks sample; no customer content

release_gate.rule: On a v1.4.0 Discover run without a customer strategy: at least 80% of the must-find use cases are found with their kind, at least 6 families appear (fewer only when fewer families have a must-find entry), no must-reject entry is selected, and the kind-floor picks average no more than 0.5 Best-of-Best below the portfolio.

matching: a candidate's tables include every required table and at least one table of each any_of group; a gold entry counts for kind recall when a matched use case carries its kind or one of its also_kinds; a must-reject entry is selected when a use case covers its tables and its name or statement matches a pattern and no unless pattern

entries.title: Late delivery risk on open order lines
entries.decision: Choose which open order lines to expedite before they miss their commit date
entries.why: Late lines cost penalties and repeat business; acting before the commit date is cheaper than apologizing after.

entries.title: Order-to-receipt flow and where lines wait
entries.decision: Fix the step between order, ship and receipt where order lines wait longest
entries.why: Cycle time is set by the slowest step; naming it tells the team where to add capacity.

entries.title: Supplier on-time performance against peers
entries.decision: Put the suppliers that deliver late more often than their peers on a review plan
entries.why: A few suppliers drive most late receipts; benchmarking against peers makes the review fair.

entries.title: Revenue change split into price, discount and volume
entries.decision: Explain each month's revenue change by price, discount and volume so the right owner acts
entries.why: Without the split, a discount-driven drop looks like a demand problem.

entries.title: Discount depth per market segment
entries.decision: Set the maximum discount per market segment and order priority
entries.why: Discounts given where they do not move volume are pure margin loss.

entries.title: Supplier choice per part from supply cost and availability
entries.decision: Pick the supplier and quantity per part that meets demand at the lowest supply cost
entries.why: Supply cost differs by supplier for the same part; the split decides the cost of goods.

entries.title: Customer segments from market segment, balance and order value
entries.decision: Pick the customer segments for each sales program
entries.why: One program for every customer wastes effort on those who would buy anyway.

entries.title: Customer lifetime value from order history
entries.decision: Set the account coverage and service level per customer value tier
entries.why: Coverage spent on low-value accounts is taken from high-value ones.

entries.title: Weekly demand forecast per part type
entries.decision: Set next weeks' supply orders per part type and brand
entries.why: Supply ordered on last week's volume runs short at peaks and long after them.

entries.title: Return risk per order line
entries.decision: Choose which order lines get a quality check before they ship
entries.why: A return costs freight both ways plus the refund; checking the riskiest lines first prevents most of it.

entries.title: Parts that depend on one supplier
entries.decision: List the parts whose supply depends on one supplier or one nation and qualify a second source
entries.why: A single-source part stops production when its supplier stops.

entries.title: Order desk staffing by day
entries.decision: Set the number of clerks per day from expected order arrivals
entries.why: Orders wait when clerks are short and clerks wait when orders are few.

entries.title: Unusual discounts per supplier and customer
entries.decision: Review the order lines whose discount breaks the usual range for their part and customer
entries.why: Out-of-range discounts are either errors or policy breaches; both lose money.

entries.title: Credit hold for customers with a negative balance
entries.decision: Choose which customers go on credit hold before their next order
entries.why: Shipping to accounts that do not pay ties up cash and ends in write-offs.

must_reject.title: Count of orders by status
must_reject.why: A count by a status column; no decision changes.

must_reject.title: List of late order lines
must_reject.why: Restates l_receiptdate > l_commitdate as a filter (T2).

must_reject.title: Revenue by nation report
must_reject.why: A sum by a dimension; no owner or action.
